record.original_question: Thatte showed that an orthogonal constructor-based rewrite system is left-sequential exactly when it is strongly sequential. Does this equivalence extend to all orthogonal term-rewriting systems? If not, is left-sequentiality decidable for orthogonal systems?

evidence.quote: Is left-sequentiality a decidable property of orthogonal systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A term rewriting system (TRS) consists of a signature of function symbols together with a set of rewrite rules l → r, where l and r are terms over the signature and a denumerable set of variables, l is not a variable, and every variable occurring in r also occurs in l. A TRS is left-linear if no variable occurs more than once in any left-hand side l. A TRS is orthogonal if it is left-linear and has no critical pairs (i.e., no two left-hand sides overlap nontrivially, including with themselves). A constructor-based TRS partitions its function symbols into defined symbols (those appearing as the root of some left-hand side) and constructors, with the restriction that every proper subterm of a left-hand side is built only from constructors and variables.

Sequentiality notions. Let Ω denote a fresh constant representing "undefined information". A Ω-term is a term over the signature extended by Ω. An index of a Ω-term t (with respect to a TRS R) is a position p in t at which Ω occurs such that every reduct (under all R-normalizing strategies) of every total instance of t requires the value at position p. A TRS R is called strongly sequential if for every Ω-term t that is not a normal form approximation, there exists a position p in t such that p is an index of t with respect to a purely syntactic, rule-blind notion of demand depending only on the left-hand sides of R. A TRS R is called left-sequential (also known as NV-sequential or sequential in the sense determined solely by left-hand sides and outermost demand) if a related but a priori weaker syntactic condition on the left-hand sides holds: for every Ω-term t that admits a reduction, some position in t can be identified as needed using only information from the left-hand sides of the rules.

Known result. For every orthogonal constructor-based TRS, left-sequentiality is equivalent to strong sequentiality.

Questions. 
(a) Does the equivalence above extend to all orthogonal TRSs: is every orthogonal left-sequential TRS strongly sequential, and conversely?
(b) Is left-sequentiality a decidable property of orthogonal TRSs? That is, does there exist an algorithm that, given a finite orthogonal TRS R, decides whether R is left-sequential?
